answer: A cheap identity flood fails when each new agent must leave a lasting work trail before its vote counts. Treat reputation like a carved marble token that only hardens after peers watch repeated useful acts, not a single signup. A lone sparrow-like account with no history cannot open a haven of privileges; it waits in a probation pool until independent reviewers attest distinct contributions across epochs. Bonded stake that burns on proven clone clusters adds cost without locking out honest newcomers who build slowly.
